with_skill.response:
A single empty `FlutterView` almost always means **Flutter's semantics tree isn't being built**, not that the Pay button lacks semantics. Android's embedding typically bridges semantics only when the OS reports an accessibility service or automation client, and `uiautomator dump` alone often doesn't trigger that. So any black-box tool will see nothing on every screen, not just checkout.

## Diagnose first (about 1 minute)

1. **Rule out timing.** Confirm the app is foregrounded and past launch, then re-dump after a short bounded wait:
   ```sh
   adb -s <serial> shell dumpsys activity activities | grep -i mResumedActivity
   adb -s <serial> shell uiautomator dump /sdcard/task-dump.xml
   adb -s <serial> exec-out cat /sdcard/task-dump.xml | grep -c 'node '
   adb -s <serial> shell rm /sdcard/task-dump.xml
   ```
2. **If it's still one node, semantics is off.** This depends on Flutter version and platform, so check against your installed SDK rather than assuming.

## Durable fix

Enable semantics from a **debug/automation entrypoint you own**, never from `main.dart`'s production path:

```dart
// lib/main_smoke.dart (or your existing test/dev entrypoint)
late final SemanticsHandle _semantics;

void main() {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  _semantics = SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics(); // held for app lifetime
  runApp(const App());
}
```

Launch with `flutter run -t lib/main_smoke.dart --flavor <flavor>`. The dump should then show real nodes, and you can tap the Pay button by its bounds and re-read to confirm the next screen. If nodes appear but Pay has no label or identifier, adding `Semantics(identifier: 'checkout-pay')` belongs in a `flutter-accessibility` change, not in permanent coordinate automation.

## Temporary fallback: coordinate tap

I can do this, but **Pay is an irreversible-class control**, so first please confirm:

- **The build points at a test/sandbox payment backend and a test account.** Which flavor and defines is it running?

Once confirmed:

```sh
adb -s <serial> exec-out screencap -p > /tmp/checkout-before.png   # locate Pay, derive center x,y
adb -s <serial> shell input tap <x> <y>
```

A zero exit code only proves the event was sent. With no tree to read, I'd verify the outcome with a bounded check: a follow-up screenshot of the expected confirmation screen plus filtered app logs (`adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof -s <appId>)`) showing the payment or navigation event.

In the smoke report, this step will be labeled **"coordinate tap, semantics tree unavailable, temporary fallback."** Coordinates will break across screen sizes, densities, and layout changes.

**My recommendation:** take the entrypoint fix. It's a few lines and unblocks every step of the smoke flow, not just this tap. If you need to proceed right now, confirm the test backend and I'll do the fallback tap.
